summary: 429s/throttling during burst on Dedicated deployment (distinguish quota enforcement vs capacity saturation)
description:
Customer-reported issue
- Customer: Zenlytics (Dedicated)
- Reported by: Customer on-call via Slack Connect + Support escalation
- Start time (customer observed): 2026-01-22 ~16:05Z
- End time (mitigated): 2026-01-22 ~17:10Z

Symptoms
- Elevated HTTP 429 responses from /v1/chat/completions during a burst in traffic (customer batch job kickoff)
- Increased queue time and p95 latency during the same window; some requests also saw 503 from gateway retry exhaustion
- Customer expected burst to be absorbed by Dedicated autoscaling (contract includes burst policy up to agreed max)

Impact
- Approx 8–15% of requests rejected with 429 for ~60 minutes
- Customer batch job delayed; customer asked if this was a quota/rate-limit change or a platform capacity issue

Environment
- Dedicated deployment: zenlytics-prod-dedicated-us-east
- Traffic shape: sudden ramp from ~45 RPS to ~140 RPS sustained for ~20 minutes; average input ~1.8k tokens, output ~300 tokens

Initial hypothesis (Support)
- Possibility A: 429 due to configured request/token rate limits (quota enforcement)
- Possibility B: 429 due to capacity saturation and overload protection (fleet saturation / autoscaling lag)

What we need to answer
1) Are 429s coming from policy/quota enforcement or from overload protection?
2) What is the owning team and correct incident taxonomy classification?
3) What immediate mitigation and longer-term fix prevents recurrence?

Customer artifacts provided
- Sample response headers (customer): x-redwood-request-id present; x-rate-limit-* headers absent
- 3 request IDs: rwreq_01HTZ7S8C3..., rwreq_01HTZ7T1A1..., rwreq_01HTZ7T8Q9...
- Customer timestamp window: 16:05Z–17:05Z

Support notes
- Customer stated they did not change their client concurrency settings; a scheduled job increased load
- Customer asked to confirm if burst pool is shared/noisy-neighbor (it is dedicated; any shedding indicates capacity/autoscaling or internal protection thresholds)
investigation_notes:
Timeline
- 16:18Z Support acknowledged; requested request IDs and exact window.
- 16:25Z Support pulled gateway logs for request IDs; saw 429 with reason=overload_shed (not quota_exceeded).
- 16:32Z Eng (Fleet) looped in for dedicated pool saturation.
- 16:40Z Routing checked router metrics: elevated fallback attempts, but primary failure mode was saturation not routing misbehavior.
- 16:55Z Fleet added temporary capacity (attach 4x GPUs) + increased autoscaler max for the dedicated pool.
- 17:10Z 429 rate returned to baseline.

Key findings (quota vs capacity)
- Dedicated quota config verified: no change; request rate limits set higher than observed RPS peak.
- 429 responses lacked rate-limit headers and included internal marker "overload_shed" in gateway logs.
- Fleet metrics indicated GPU utilization pegged at >95% with queue depth spikes; autoscaler scale-out lagged by ~12–18 minutes due to provisioning delay + conservative scale-up thresholds.
- Router fallback_reason metrics (from recent instrumentation) showed capacity/health-based fallback attempts spiking, but no evidence of policy-based throttling.

Most likely root cause
- Dedicated pool capacity saturation during burst + autoscaling lag => gateway load shedding generated 429s.

Contributing factors
- Autoscaler max was set to standard (non-burst) ceiling for this tenant, despite contract addendum for burst.
- Provisioning delay in us-east GPU pool created a longer-than-expected scale-out.

What we told the customer (high confidence)
- This was NOT a quota enforcement event.
- The 429s were generated by overload protection while the dedicated pool was saturating.
- We mitigated by increasing capacity and raising the autoscaling ceiling; we are updating autoscaling config to match burst commitment.
proposed_incident_taxonomy:
v1 classification proposal
- incident_type: Capacity / Fleet shortage
- subtype: Dedicated pool saturation (autoscaling lag / provisioning delay)
- primary owner: Infra/Fleet (Vanessa Ortiz)
- secondary/consulted: Smart Routing (Mina Haddad) for fallback behavior + SRE (Rafael Mendes) for SLA tracking

Notes on classification boundary
- Not classified as "Auth/RBAC" or "Quota/Rate Limit" because the signals showed overload shedding and no quota headers.
- Routing was involved only as a mitigation/fallback path; the triggering constraint was fleet capacity.
customer_communication:
Customer-facing summary (approved by Support)
- We observed overload protection triggering while your Dedicated pool was saturating during a burst in traffic.
- The elevated 429s were not due to a change in your quota or a new rate-limit policy.
- Mitigation applied: increased capacity in your Dedicated pool and raised autoscaling max to align to the burst commitment.
- Next steps: we will adjust autoscaling thresholds to react faster for your workload shape, and we will add an alert to detect saturation earlier.

Customer questions captured
- Can you guarantee burst absorption up to X RPS? (Answer: we can align autoscaling max and pre-warm capacity for scheduled bursts; recommend scheduled burst window notice.)
- Why did 429 happen instead of queuing? (Answer: overload protection preserves tail latency and prevents runaway queue growth.)

resolution: Resolved via capacity mitigation on Dedicated pool and autoscaler max increase. Confirmed 429s were overload shedding due to capacity saturation (not quota enforcement).
follow_up_actions:
1) Fleet: Update tenant autoscaler config to match burst commitment (max + faster scale-up thresholds) and document in tenant config change log.
2) SRE: Add alert for dedicated pool saturation leading indicators (queue depth + sustained GPU >90%) to page Fleet before shedding triggers.
3) Support/CS: Provide customer guidance on scheduled bursts (optional pre-warm request + recommended ramp pattern).
4) Routing: Confirm fallback behavior during saturation does not amplify customer-visible 429s; validate graceful degradation messaging.

- Support: Dev Patel / Owen Phillips
